intro: — please see below the discrepancies we found while creating the test cases for this ticket. We write our tests from section 7 and the acceptance criteria here, so anywhere the build differs the step fails on purpose. Several of these are already in section 8 as outstanding, so they are confirmation rather than news.

items.text: The breakpoint has three different values. AC-19 and AC-20 both say 1024px, section 8 records the repo as being on 900px, and the code is on neither — header.js uses matchMedia('(min-width: 1200px)') with the matching desktop block in header.css. The boundary steps fail until this is settled. Which number is correct?

The class names differ from the spec. Section 7 names .mm-a, .mm-b, .mm-a2 and the rest of the .ufs-* / .mm-* taxonomy; develop ships .nav-*. The geometry underneath is already right — the 1fr 1fr 1fr 260px, 1.8fr 1fr 1fr 260px and 1fr 1fr grids are all in header.css exactly as specified — so this is names only, but every step that selects a panel by class fails on it.

There is no .is-open class. AC-6 and AC-7 put it on the panel and the trigger; it doesn't appear anywhere in header.js. Open state is carried by aria-expanded on the section instead, which works, but it isn't what the spec says to look for.

The dark and glass contexts don't exist. AC-4 asks for them and AC-18 asks for contrast checks in them; neither the --dark nor the --glass modifier is in header.css yet, so those steps have nothing to check.
Two accessibility gaps, found in the code rather than the spec.
bullets: The "View more" button has aria-expanded but no aria-label, so its only accessible name is the literal text "View more" — identical for every category in the drawer, which is the ambiguity AC-17 exists to prevent.
There is no focus trap in the drawer. It registers a keydown handler for Escape only: no Tab handling and no focus return to the hamburger, so both halves of AC-16 are unimplemented.

items.text: One row of the section 8 table is out of date in the opposite direction. It records the mobile pattern as a "simple stack", with the drawer, the single-open accordion and "View more" all still to build. All three are built and working on develop today, with the cut-off at four links (DRAWER_VISIBLE_LINKS = 4) and .is-extra used exactly as AC-11 names it. Worth correcting so the table stops describing finished work as outstanding.
